title: A full Frobenius flag in the constructible Weil heart at a point
statement:
Fix a prime power $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and an isomorphism $\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$, as in [def-weil-punctual-weights]. Let $\mathcal F$ be any constructible $\Qlb$-Weil sheaf on $\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ in the raw/common-stage heart of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Let $(V,F)$ be its finite-dimensional geometric fibre with invertible local geometric Frobenius, using [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace; lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence], and put $d=\dim_{\Qlb}V$. There is a full filtration by constructible Weil subsheaves
$$0=\mathcal F_0\subset\mathcal F_1\subset\cdots\subset\mathcal F_d=\mathcal F$$
whose fibre at stage $j$ has dimension $j$. Each quotient has one-dimensional fibre with Frobenius scalar $\alpha_j\in\Qlb^\times$, and is punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $2\log_q|\iota(\alpha_j)|$. Its geometric fibre filtration is an $F$-invariant full flag, and $F$ restricts to an automorphism on every flag space and quotient. All these spaces, maps and Weil isomorphisms can be represented simultaneously at a single finite coefficient extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in the raw coefficient heart, with the specified fibre and point-transport identifications. In particular $\mathcal F$ is mixed. The conclusion includes nontrivial Jordan blocks, requires no reality or semisimplicity hypothesis, and for $V=0$ gives the empty filtration. It holds with $k_0$ replaced by any finite extension, using that field's cardinality as $q$.
